messages.author: bc4b077798ca353e
messages.subject: How to analyze density estimates?
parts:
Hello,

I have a question regarding the use of distance-based density estimates for =

analysis of a 4-year experiment on forest fuel treatments. The experiment=20
has 4 treatments with 3 replicates in each treatment group (forest=20
stands). Treatment groups are: Control, Prescribed Fire, Thinning, and=20
Thinning+Fire. 2001 was a pre-treatment year, 2002 a transition year (some=20
replicates thinned prior) and 2003 and 2004 are post-treatment years (all=20
treatments finished prior to surveys). Response variables are the counts=20
of different bird species (each species is analyzed separate).

6 point transects were surveyed 3x each year in each replicate (thus 18=20
visits/replicate/year). Data were collected in 10m bins up to 50m

Because of low sample sizes, I have used MCDS to estimate the global model, =

and then post-stratified using both (1) Treatment_Year combo (4 densities=20
per year) and (2) Replicate_Year combo (12 densities year) to get density=20
estimates. For the strata, this leaves me with density estimates that have =

variances associated with them. My understanding is that because I used=20
the global model to estimate (1) and (2), the density estimates are not=20
independent. I have been referred to p. 85 in Buckland et al. (2001) for=20
how to correct the variances for each strata estimate.

I am pretty comfortable with the modeling of the data. I can use=20
continuous covariates - but for factor covariates (year, treatment, obs) I=20
often get convergence failure. =20

My questions are in regards to the comparison of the density estimates.

Questions:

1. On p. 86, var^n_i is required (eq.3.111). I cannot find this in the=20
output. I'm assuming it is not the encounter rate. Is there a way to get=20
this output, or do I just do the calcs by hand?

2. The na=EFve way of analyzing my data would be a repeated-measures ANOVA =

on the count data. Do I run this ANOVA with the distance-based density=20
estimates as is, or do I need to incorporate the uncertainty of the=20
estimates? If so, how? Or is there a better way?

3. For all species, there have been no significant differences in=20
parameters (p, n/k, etc) in each strata. Does this mean I could do an=20
ANOVA on the index values (raw count data)?

4. For half of my species, I have "evasive movement" and cannot manipulate =

the data to fit curves. On the detection histogram it looks like cell-
phone bars (increasing with distance). It seems like there is no solution =

to this. Do I just run an ANOVA on the raw count data for these data (and=20
mention the caveats)? =20

5. Finally, I could do z-tests on the Treatment_Year combo, but it seems=20
like I would be doing an awful lot of multiple comparisons (4=20
densities/year x 4 years =3D 16 things to compare). The Treatment_Replicate=
=20
stratum is so I can run ANOVAs.

Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

cheers,

Andy Amacher
PhD Student
Dept ESPM, UC Berkeley
aama...@nature.berkeley.edu
